cards.back: Old Testament · Law
God creates, judges, and begins a people through Abraham.

Genesis 1:1 (NIV)
In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
Old Testament · Law
God redeems Israel from slavery and makes them his people at Sinai.

Exodus 20:2 (NIV)
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery.
Old Testament · Law
A holy God makes a way for a sinful people to live near him.

Leviticus 19:2 (NIV)
Be holy because I, the Lord your God, am holy.
Old Testament · Law
God leads Israel through the wilderness, in their wandering and his faithfulness.

Numbers 6:24 (NIV)
The Lord bless you and keep you.
Old Testament · Law
Moses retells the law and calls Israel to love the Lord with all their heart.

Deuteronomy 6:5 (NIV)
Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.
Old Testament · History
God keeps his promise and brings Israel into the land.

Joshua 1:9 (NIV)
Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged, for the Lord your God will be with you wherever you go.
Old Testament · History
Israel cycles through sin, oppression, crying out, and God's rescue.

Judges 21:25 (NIV)
In those days Israel had no king; everyone did as they saw fit.
Old Testament · History
God's kindness works through ordinary faithfulness in the line of David.

Ruth 1:16 (NIV)
Where you go I will go, and where you stay I will stay. Your people will be my people and your God my God.
Old Testament · History
God raises up Samuel, Saul, and David, and looks at the heart.

1 Samuel 16:7 (NIV)
People look at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.
Old Testament · History
David's reign, his sin, and God's covenant promise of an everlasting throne.

2 Samuel 7:16 (NIV)
Your house and your kingdom will endure forever before me; your throne will be established forever.
Old Testament · History
Solomon's glory, the divided kingdom, and the call to listen to God's word.

1 Kings 8:27 (NIV)
The heavens, even the highest heaven, cannot contain you. How much less this temple I have built!
Old Testament · History
The kingdoms fall; God remains faithful even in exile.

2 Kings 17:13 (NIV)
The Lord warned Israel and Judah through all his prophets and seers: 'Turn from your evil ways.'
Old Testament · History
A priestly retelling of Israel's story, centered on worship and David's line.

1 Chronicles 16:34 (NIV)
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; his love endures forever.
Old Testament · History
The temple, revival, and the hope of return after judgment.

2 Chronicles 7:14 (NIV)
If my people, who are called by my name, will humble themselves and pray and seek my face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, and I will forgive their sin and will heal their land.
Old Testament · History
God brings a remnant home and restores worship around his Word.

Ezra 7:10 (NIV)
Ezra had devoted himself to the study and observance of the Law of the Lord, and to teaching its decrees and laws in Israel.
Old Testament · History
God uses Nehemiah to rebuild the wall and call the people back to the Word.

Nehemiah 8:10 (NIV)
The joy of the Lord is your strength.
Old Testament · History
God quietly preserves his people in Persia when they seem forgotten.

Esther 4:14 (NIV)
And who knows but that you have come to your royal position for such a time as this?
Old Testament · Poetry / Wisdom
A righteous sufferer wrestles with God and finds that God is wise and good.

Job 19:25 (NIV)
I know that my redeemer lives, and that in the end he will stand on the earth.
Old Testament · Poetry / Wisdom
Songs of prayer and praise for every season of the soul.

Psalm 23:1 (NIV)
The Lord is my shepherd, I lack nothing.
Old Testament · Poetry / Wisdom
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom for everyday life.

Proverbs 1:7 (NIV)
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
Old Testament · Poetry / Wisdom
Life 'under the sun' is empty unless we fear God and keep his commands.

Ecclesiastes 12:13 (NIV)
Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the duty of all mankind.
Old Testament · Poetry / Wisdom
A joyful, faithful picture of marital love as a gift from God.

Song of Songs 2:16 (NIV)
My beloved is mine and I am his.
Old Testament · Major Prophets
The Holy One of Israel judges sin and promises a coming Servant-King.

Isaiah 9:6 (NIV)
For to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government will be on his shoulders.
Old Testament · Major Prophets
God judges Judah and promises a new covenant written on the heart.

Jeremiah 31:33 (NIV)
I will put my law in their minds and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
Old Testament · Major Prophets
Honest grief after Jerusalem falls, with hope in God's mercies.

Lamentations 3:22–23 (NIV)
Because of the Lord's great love we are not consumed, for his compassions never fail. They are new every morning.
Old Testament · Major Prophets
God is still present in exile and promises a new heart and a new temple.

Ezekiel 36:26 (NIV)
I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit in you.
Old Testament · Major Prophets
God rules the nations; his kingdom will never be destroyed.

Daniel 7:14 (NIV)
His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom is one that will never be destroyed.
Old Testament · Minor Prophets
God's faithful love pursues an unfaithful people.

Hosea 6:6 (NIV)
For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and acknowledgment of God rather than burnt offerings.
Old Testament · Minor Prophets
A locust plague becomes a call to repent and a promise of the Spirit.

Joel 2:13 (NIV)
Rend your heart and not your garments. Return to the Lord your God, for he is gracious and compassionate.
Old Testament · Minor Prophets
God calls for justice and true worship, not empty religion.

Amos 5:24 (NIV)
But let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream!
Old Testament · Minor Prophets
God judges Edom's pride and promises that the kingdom will be the Lord's.

Obadiah 1:15 (NIV)
The day of the Lord is near for all nations.
Old Testament · Minor Prophets
God's compassion reaches even Nineveh, and he is patient with a reluctant prophet.

Jonah 2:9 (NIV)
Salvation comes from the Lord.
Old Testament · Minor Prophets
God requires justice, mercy, and humility, and promises a ruler from Bethlehem.

Micah 5:2 (NIV)
But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel.
Old Testament · Minor Prophets
God is slow to anger, yet he will not leave the guilty unpunished.

Nahum 1:7 (NIV)
The Lord is good, a refuge in times of trouble. He cares for those who trust in him.
Old Testament · Minor Prophets
A prophet asks why God allows injustice, and learns to live by faith.

Habakkuk 2:4 (NIV)
The righteous person will live by his faithfulness.
Old Testament · Minor Prophets
The Day of the Lord is near; God will judge and then rejoice over his people.

Zephaniah 3:17 (NIV)
The Lord your God is with you, the Mighty Warrior who saves. He will take great delight in you; in his love he will no longer rebuke you, but will rejoice over you with singing.
Old Testament · Minor Prophets
God calls the returned exiles to put his house first.

Haggai 2:9 (NIV)
The glory of this present house will be greater than the glory of the former house.
Old Testament · Minor Prophets
Visions of cleansing, a humble King, and the Lord coming to his people.

Zechariah 9:9 (NIV)
See, your king comes to you, righteous and victorious, lowly and riding on a donkey.
Old Testament · Minor Prophets
God still loves his people and promises a messenger before the Lord comes.

Malachi 3:1 (NIV)
I will send my messenger, who will prepare the way before me.
New Testament · Gospels
Jesus is the promised Messiah, the Son of David who fulfills the Scriptures.

Matthew 1:21 (NIV)
She will give birth to a son, and you are to give him the name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.
New Testament · Gospels
Jesus is the suffering Son of God who came not to be served but to serve.

Mark 10:45 (NIV)
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.
New Testament · Gospels
Jesus is the Savior of all kinds of people, announced with joy and historical care.

Luke 19:10 (NIV)
For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.
New Testament · Gospels
Jesus is the eternal Word made flesh, the Son who gives life.

John 20:31 (NIV)
But these are written that you may believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name.
New Testament · History
The risen Jesus sends his Spirit and his church to the ends of the earth.

Acts 1:8 (NIV)
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.
New Testament · Paul's Letters
The gospel of God's righteousness given by grace through faith in Christ.

Romans 1:16 (NIV)
For I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God that brings salvation to everyone who believes.
New Testament · Paul's Letters
The gospel shapes a messy church into a holy, loving body.

1 Corinthians 15:3–4 (NIV)
Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures.
New Testament · Paul's Letters
God's power is shown in weakness, and ministry is a ministry of reconciliation.

2 Corinthians 5:17 (NIV)
Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!
New Testament · Paul's Letters
We are justified by faith, not by works of the law, and called to walk by the Spirit.

Galatians 2:16 (NIV)
A person is not justified by the works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ.
New Testament · Paul's Letters
God's grace in Christ makes a new people, the church, for his glory.

Ephesians 2:8–9 (NIV)
For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith—and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God—not by works, so that no one can boast.
New Testament · Paul's Letters
Joy in Christ, even in prison, and a call to have the mind of Christ.

Philippians 2:5–7 (NIV)
In your relationships with one another, have the same mindset as Christ Jesus: Who, being in very nature God, did not consider equality with God something to be used to his own advantage; rather, he made himself nothing.
New Testament · Paul's Letters
Christ is supreme over all, and we are complete in him.

Colossians 1:15 (NIV)
The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation.
New Testament · Paul's Letters
Live in holiness and hope as you wait for Jesus' return.

1 Thessalonians 4:16–17 (NIV)
For the Lord himself will come down from heaven, with a loud command, with the voice of the archangel and with the trumpet call of God, and the dead in Christ will rise first. After that, we who are still alive and are left will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. And so we will be with the Lord forever.
New Testament · Paul's Letters
Stand firm; do not be shaken by rumors about the Day of the Lord.

2 Thessalonians 2:16–17 (NIV)
May our Lord Jesus Christ himself and God our Father... encourage your hearts and strengthen you in every good deed and word.
New Testament · Paul's Letters
Guard the gospel and order the church with godliness.

1 Timothy 3:15 (NIV)
God's household, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.
New Testament · Paul's Letters
Finish the race; the Scriptures are God-breathed and make you complete.

2 Timothy 3:16–17 (NIV)
All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting and training in righteousness, so that the servant of God may be thoroughly equipped for every good work.
New Testament · Paul's Letters
Sound doctrine produces a well-ordered, good life in the church and home.

Titus 2:11–12 (NIV)
For the grace of God has appeared that offers salvation to all people. It teaches us to say 'No' to ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live self-controlled, upright and godly lives in this present age.
New Testament · Paul's Letters
The gospel turns a runaway slave and his owner into brothers in Christ.

Philemon 1:17–18 (NIV)
So if you consider me a partner, welcome him as you would welcome me. If he has done you any wrong or owes you anything, charge it to me.
New Testament · General Letters
Jesus is better than every shadow in the old covenant.

Hebrews 1:1–2 (NIV)
In the past God spoke to our ancestors through the prophets at many times and in various ways, but in these last days he has spoken to us by his Son.
New Testament · General Letters
Genuine faith works itself out in a life of wisdom and love.

James 1:22 (NIV)
Do not merely listen to the word, and so deceive yourselves. Do what it says.
New Testament · General Letters
Hope and holiness for exiles who follow a suffering, risen Christ.

1 Peter 2:9 (NIV)
But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's special possession.
New Testament · General Letters
Grow in grace; remember that the Lord will surely come.

2 Peter 3:18 (NIV)
But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
New Testament · General Letters
Those who belong to Jesus walk in the light, love the brothers, and believe the truth.

1 John 1:9 (NIV)
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.
New Testament · General Letters
Walk in love and do not welcome teachers who deny that Jesus came in the flesh.

2 John 1:6 (NIV)
And this is love: that we walk in obedience to his commands.
New Testament · General Letters
Welcome faithful workers and copy what is good, not what is evil.

3 John 1:4 (NIV)
I have no greater joy than to hear that my children are walking in the truth.
New Testament · General Letters
Contend for the faith once for all entrusted to God's people.

Jude 1:24 (NIV)
To him who is able to keep you from stumbling and to present you before his glorious presence without fault and with great joy.
New Testament · Prophecy / Apocalypse
The risen Christ rules, comforts his churches, and will make all things new.

Revelation 21:5 (NIV)
He who was seated on the throne said, 'I am making everything new!'

For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith—and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God—not by works, so that no one can boast.

(End times)

Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

(Trinity / baptism)

These commandments that I give you today are to be on your hearts. Impress them on your children. Talk about them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.

(Parenthood)

Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own; you were bought at a price. Therefore honor God with your bodies.

(Purity)

But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

(Holy Spirit)
God's undeserved favor. In salvation, God makes us alive with Christ as a gift, not as a wage (Ephesians 2:8–9).
Christ's sacrifice turns aside God's righteous wrath against sin. Romans 3:25 speaks of Christ as a 'sacrifice of atonement' in the NIV; many literal translations say 'propitiation.'
God's declaration that a sinner is righteous, freely, through faith in Jesus — not by works of the law (Romans 3:24).
Turning from sin to God. Jesus joins it to faith: 'Repent and believe the good news' (Mark 1:15).
Trusting God's promise and God's Son — receiving a gift, not earning a wage (Ephesians 2:8).
Being made holy. It is God's will that we be sanctified, including in how we handle our bodies (1 Thessalonians 4:3).
A solemn, binding promise. The Bible's story is held together by the covenants God makes and keeps, fulfilled in the new covenant in Jesus' blood.
There is one God in three Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Each is fully God; they are not three gods and not one Person wearing three masks.
The good news of first importance: Christ died for our sins, was buried, and was raised on the third day (1 Corinthians 15:3–4).
The work by which God and sinners are made at one through the blood of Jesus.
The view that men and women are equal in dignity and not interchangeable in every calling — as taught at Grace Life and by teachers such as John Piper and Tony Evans.
The promised covenant written on the heart, sealed in Jesus' blood, bringing forgiveness and the Spirit (Jeremiah 31; Luke 22:20).
